analysis:
Documentation-only PR touching docs/architecture/hardware-support.md (new head lines 318-340 describing cold-load FIFO release, awaitReleasedLoads and the prompt token store memory accounting) and docs/architecture/inference.md (new paragraph around head lines 1030-1047 describing PromptTokenCache and ChatTemplateLoopRewrites). The rest of the hardware-support.md diff is a line-shift from the inserted block. The unit with start_line 1 of that file is the head text, with no other substantive differences visible.

No code, key handling, wire format, attestation or authorization controls are changed, so no regression against TB-002, TB-003, TB-007 or TB-011 is introduced by this diff.

Security-relevant claims for later review (the code is not supplied here): (1) PromptTokenCache reuse is described as 'never crossing a cache scope', scoped to the prefix-cache scope. Related to T-041, since a shared token cache keyed only by piece text could create a cross-tenant timing/sharing oracle (the same-account SEC-035 class). The doc says scope-bound, and the coordinator-authored cacheSalt from T-041 is the expected scope source. The implementation should be verified to key on that salt and not on caller-controlled prompt_cache_key/user. (2) The token store is ordinary process heap, bounded at 32 MiB by default per tokenizer via DARKBLOOM_TTFT_PROMPT_CACHE_MB. It holds token IDs derived from plaintext prompts (A-001) in process memory only, consistent with the T-014/T-011 process-memory posture, and is not described as persisted to disk. (3) Cold-load FIFO release lets requests overtake. This is an availability/ordering change that the doc says still passes through the pending-load gates. No fail-open path is documented, and the memory gate is stated to remain authoritative.

No finding. If the implementing PRs are separate, the threat model might add a note that PromptTokenCache is a new in-memory derivative of prompts and must stay scope-keyed.
